09.3Chapter 9 · LLM Optimization in Practice

Common optimization trade-offs

Practice me "perfect" configuration dhoondhne se zyada effort ye decide karne me lagta hai ki kaunsi optimization techniques apply karni hain. Har technique ke saath ek trade-off hota hai — aur use apne scenario ke hisaab se adapt karna hi real-world LLM serving optimization ka essence hai. Book paanch trade-offs batati hai.

1. Throughput vs latency

Higher throughput aam taur par batching aur scheduling optimizations se aati hai jo GPU ko behtar utilize karti hain. Lekin bade batches waiting time introduce karte hain, jo per-request latency badhata hai. Interactive applications (jaise chatbots) low latency favor karte hain, jabki offline ya batch inference high throughput favor karta hai. Practice me throughput improvement prioritize karo, lekin latency ko acceptable range me rakho — aur yaad rakho, kuch techniques (jaise distributed serving) latency ko throughput se zyada priority deti hain.

2. Memory efficiency vs model quality

Quantization ya weight compression GPU memory usage kam karta hai aur KV cache capacity badhata hai — lekin isse chhoti accuracy losses ya token instability aa sakti hai. Sahi balance (jaise 4-bit vs 8-bit quantization) is par depend karta hai ki aap quality degradation ke mukable performance gain ko kitna tolerate kar sakte ho. Chapter 9 ke experiments me AWQ 4-bit ne throughput 2.7x badhaya — lekin har workload me itna aggressive quantization acceptable nahi hota; quality check hamesha saath me karo.

3. Hardware utilization vs flexibility

Aggressive tuning (batch size, tensor parallelism, cache size) ek specific GPU ya workload ke liye performance maximize kar sakti hai. Lekin ye settings aksar doosre hardware ya traffic patterns par generalize nahi hoti. Zyada flexible setup efficiency ke kuch percentage points trade karta hai, portability aur robustness ke badle. Ek specific setup ke liye over-optimized configuration doosre setup par kharab perform kar sakti hai ya fail bhi ho sakti hai — isliye overfitting se bacho.

4. Vertical vs horizontal scaling

Vertical scaling (distributed serving) bade models enable karta hai aur GPUs par inference spread karke latency kam kar sakta hai. Horizontal scaling (multiple single-GPU replicas) total throughput aur fault tolerance improve karta hai. Practice me most production systems horizontal scaling par focus karte hain — aur Chapter 9 ke numbers yehi dikhate hain: chaar independent replicas ne distributed 4-GPU setup se lagbhag teen guna throughput diya. Vertical scaling tabhi chuno jab model single GPU me fit na ho ya latency priority ho.

5. Static optimization vs adaptive serving

Static configurations predictable hoti hain lekin limited — woh ek specific GPU ya workload par overfit kar sakti hain. Adaptive runtime optimization live traffic aur hardware metrics ke hisaab se batch size, cache policy ya scheduling ko dynamically adjust karta hai. Ye serving frameworks ka agla stage hai: self-optimizing systems jo performance ko automatically balance karte hain. Modern frameworks pehle se hi startup par achhi settings infer karne lage hain — aur aane wale samay me ye adaptivity aur badhegi.

Chapter 9 ke key takeaways

  • Optimization universal "best" configuration ke baare me nahi hai — dominant bottleneck samjho aur sahi technique sahi level par apply karo (hardware, model, ya scheduling).
  • Shuruaat apne scenario se karo: business use case, traffic pattern aur performance target clearly define karo, phir tune karo.
  • Representative test datasets aur meaningful metrics banao jo real user workloads aur performance goals ko reflect karein — ye meaningful optimization ke liye critical hain.
  • Pehle general throughput optimizations se strong baseline banao, phir workload-specific tuning apply karo.
  • Targeted techniques traffic type ke hisaab se chuno: long-context (prefill-heavy) workloads ke liye LMCache, long-output (decode-heavy) workloads ke liye speculative decoding.
  • Throughput aur latency ko priorities ke hisaab se balance karo: per request zyada memory allocate karke ya concurrency limit karke latency kam kar sakte ho, total capacity ke cost par.
  • Distributed serving selectively use karo — khaas taur par jab model size single-GPU limits se zyada ho ya low latency priority ho.
  • Most cases me single GPUs par chalana aur horizontally multiple replicas se scale karna behtar throughput aur simplicity deta hai.
  • Overspecific static configurations se bacho — fixed KV cache block sizes ya hardware-tied parameters ek GPU type par overfit kar sakte hain.
Yaad rakho: effective serving optimization ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — ye continuous experimentation, measurement aur trade-off analysis hai, jo real user scenarios par rooted ho. Har experiment se intuition banti hai, aur wahi intuition agle optimization decision ko tez aur sahi banati hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — LLM Optimization in Practice
← Previous09.2 · Qwen3-14B end-to-end optimization (8 steps)→ Next10.1 · Semantic caching
10.1Chapter 10 · Advancements in LLM Serving

Semantic caching

Chapter 7 me routing replica level par thi — load balancer requests ko multiple model replicas me baant ta tha, aur prefix caching ke saath KV-cache-aware load balancing aayi. Ab serving systems semantics ke level par kaam karne lagi hain: semantic-aware routing, caching aur retrieval exact prompts par based nahi hoti, balki embeddings aur vector search use karke same intent wale prompts ko pehchanti hai. Isse aur zyada cache hits, smarter decisions (reasoning enable karna hai ya nahi), agentic tool filtering, aur model-endpoint level par model selection milti hai — sirf replica level par nahi.

Semantic routing kyun? Chaar reasons

1. LLM call hi avoid karo: "How long is the flight from Seattle to Hawaii?" aur "Tell me how many hours it takes to fly from Seattle to Hawaii" — dono ka matlab same hai. Dobara LLM call karna, khaas taur par external LLM ko, overkill hai: paise ki barbaadi aur unnecessary latency. Semantic caching pehle ke query results store karke samajhti hai ki queries similar hain, aur cached response de deti hai bina extra LLM call ke.

2. Sahi model aur reasoning chuno: har naye prompt ke liye bhi bada model ya reasoning on karna zaroori nahi hota. Semantic router ek lightweight encoder model se jaldi decide kar sakta hai ki prompt complex hai ya nahi — aur us hisaab se sabse advanced model call kare ya reasoning enable kare.

3. Small fine-tuned models ko route karo: companies realize kar rahi hain ki task-specific, fine-tuned small language models (SLMs, lagbhag 8–32 billion parameters) kai tasks me giant general-purpose LLMs ke barabar ya behtar perform kar sakte hain — behtar reliability aur SLA/SLO control ke liye kam latency ke saath. Semantic router query ko samajh kar request ko appropriate model endpoint par route karta hai.

4. Agentic tool filtering: agentic settings me routing service request ko sirf forward nahi karti — woh first-level tool filtering bhi kar sakti hai, taaki model ko saare available tools expose na karne padein. Ye increasingly Model Context Protocol (MCP) ke through hota hai, jahan tools structured schemas, permissions aur metadata ke saath register hote hain. Router user request ke hisaab se sirf relevant tools ka chhota subset model ko deta hai — prompt overhead kam, latency behtar, aur unintended tool use ka risk kam. Routing service security, policy aur compliance checks ka central enforcement point bhi banti hai.

Semantic router kaise kaam karta hai — paanch steps

Step 1 — PII masking: raw user inputs me aksar sensitive data hota hai — naam, address, contact information, credit card number, ya health details. PII ko remove ya obfuscate karna crucial hai, taaki downstream logs, caches aur routing decisions kabhi private information expose na karein. Ye router ya gateway me hota hai. PII model aam taur par ek chhota encoder model hota hai jo privacy-sensitive entities par named entity recognition (NER) ke liye fine-tune kiya gaya hota hai — output me har entity ki position (start/end), label (jaise PERSON, EMAIL) aur confidence hoti hai. Positional information se prompt me PII tokens ko placeholders jaise <NAME_1> aur <Email_1> se replace kar diya jaata hai. Kai cases me regex methods bhi NER model ko complement karti hain.

Step 2 — Embedding: embedding model har prompt ko numbers ki list me transform karta hai — jaise length 768 ka embedding vector. Similar meaning wale prompts ke embedding vectors similar hote hain: "forget my login" aur "reset password" ke vectors similar honge, jabki "forget my login" aur "create me a draft article" ke vectors bahut alag honge.

Step 3 — Vector search aur cache hit: embedding vector se vector search karke pehle store kiye gaye prompt-response pairs dhoondhe jaate hain. Agar bahut close match mil jaaye, to cached response turant return ho jaati hai — bina kisi extra LLM call ke.

Step 4 — Tool filtering: agar bahut saare tools hain, to vector search se list narrow ki ja sakti hai — saare tools LLM ko bhejna expensive hota hai.

Step 5 — Model selection classifier: embedding vector ko ek chhote classifier ka input banaya jaata hai jo decide karta hai kaunsa LLM call karna hai aur reasoning enable karni hai ya nahi. Classifier ke output label ke hisaab se appropriate LLM invoke hota hai — jaise complex reasoning ke liye external state-of-the-art model, specific tasks ke liye medium-sized internal model, ya simple question ke liye chhota internal model.

Yaad rakho: semantic caching exact-match prefix caching se ek level upar hai — ye intent match karti hai, text nahi. Isi liye ye paraphrased questions, model selection, reasoning decisions aur tool filtering — sab ko ek hi routing layer me laa sakti hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Advancements in LLM Serving
← Previous09.3 · Common optimization trade-offs→ Next10.2 · Performance profiling strategies
10.2Chapter 10 · Advancements in LLM Serving

Performance profiling strategies

LLM serving mehenge hain, isliye workload profiling ki kala gehri ho gayi hai. Pichhli generation ke chhote predictive models me ye itna critical nahi tha, lekin aaj scale par serving ka matlab hai ki ek percentage point ka improvement bhi infrastructure cost me millions of dollars bacha sakta hai. Aakhri kuch percentage points ab optional luxury nahi, operational necessity hain. Is section me seekhenge ki LLM inference workloads ko profile karke performance hotspots kaise identify karein, aur low-level kernel optimization throughput aur latency ko kaise improve karta hai. Book custom CUDA ya Triton kernels likhne me deep dive nahi karti, lekin ye samajhna essential hai ki woh kya optimize karte hain aur profiling system-level observations ko kernel-level behavior se kaise jodti hai.

Profiling ki teen layers

Serving layer (sabse upar): yahan throughput, TTFT, ITL, GPU utilization aur memory utilization jaise metrics milte hain, aur adjustments karke serving performance improve karke SLA/SLO targets achieve karte ho. Ye layer aapko ab tak ke chapters se achhi tarah samajh aa gayi hogi.

Framework layer: deep-learning frameworks (jaise PyTorch) ke andar model operations ka graph hota hai. PyTorch Profiler jaise tools se inspect kar sakte ho ki specific operators (building-block computations jaise matmul, attention, ya layernorm) kaise execute hote hain, data CPU aur GPU ke beech kaise move hota hai, aur pipeline computation aur input/output ko efficiently overlap kar rahi hai ya nahi. Example: operator execution timeline batata hai kaunsa operator GPU execution time dominate kar raha hai — phir us operator ko target karke alag kernel implementation se replace kar sakte ho. Doosra example: GPU mostly idle hai, CPU side ka kaam khatam hone ka wait kar raha hai — tab GPU utilization improve karne ke liye CPU workloads ko async processes me move karke critical path se hata sakte ho.

Runtime layer (sabse neeche): model aakhir me operators ki sequence ke roop me execute hota hai (matmul, attention, layernorm), aur har operator ek ya zyada CUDA kernels me expand hota hai jo asal math karte hain. In kernels ke andar kya hota hai, ye samajhna crucial hai, kyunki yahan ki inefficiencies aksar explain karti hain ki framework level par ek operator expensive kyun dikh raha hai. Nsight Systems common starting point hai — system-wide performance-analysis timeline deta hai, major bottlenecks identify karne ke liye. Nsight Compute iske ulta kernel-level details ka microarchitectural view deta hai. Example: Nsight Systems reveal kar sakta hai ki GPU utilization high dikhne ke bawjood kernels ke beech bade idle gaps hain — host kernels ko bahut slowly launch kar raha hai, ya data transfers computation ke saath overlap nahi ho rahe. Fix: ek se zyada CUDA streams use karke data copies ko computation ke saath overlap karna, taaki GPU busy rahe. Agar ek kernel bottleneck hai aur overall time dominate kar raha hai, to Nsight Compute batata hai kyun — low thread occupancy ya frequent memory stalls. Example: attention softmax kernel sabse slow ho sakta hai, kyunki woh bade intermediate tensors ko shared memory me rakhne ke bajaye global memory se baar-baar load karta hai. Is information se us kernel ko directly target kar sakte ho — memory access patterns optimize karke, block/grid configuration adjust karke, ya zyada efficient fused kernel se replace karke.

Decision flowchart: symptom se root cause tak

Profiling ki asli challenge hai pata hona ki kaunsa tool kab use karna hai aur ek layer se doosri par kaise move karna hai. Book ka decision flowchart iska practical roadmap deta hai: shuruaat Nsight Systems se — top-down, system-wide timeline. Ye batata hai ki GPU asal me bottleneck hai ya asli issue CPU overhead, data loading ya I/O me hai. Agar GPU underutilized hai, to PyTorch Profiler (CPU Mode) se host side par time kahan spend ho raha hai ye dekho — slow preprocessing, Python dispatch overhead, ya serialization work. Agar GPU busy hai lekin latency phir bhi unexpectedly high hai, to PyTorch Profiler (CUDA Mode) se GPU time ko high-level PyTorch operators par attribute karo — attention, matmul, layernorm, ya koi aur operator dominate kar raha hai, ye pinpoint karo. Agar ek operator ke andar ek kernel most time le raha hai, to Nsight Compute se microarchitectural details me drill karo — warp occupancy, memory stalls, tensor-core utilization — aur decide karo kernel ko tune karna hai, replace karna hai, ya fuse karna hai. Agar koi single kernel dominate nahi kar raha, to issue aam taur par launch overhead, missing overlapping, ya synchronization se related hota hai — tab Nsight Systems ki timeline par wapas jao.

Yaad rakho: profiling me tool ka naam yaad rakhna kaafi nahi hai — layer ka order yaad rakho: serving metrics se symptom, framework profiler se operator, runtime profiler se kernel. Har layer agle layer ka sawaal batati hai, aur bina order ke profiling me kho jaana aasan hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Advancements in LLM Serving
← Previous10.1 · Semantic caching→ Next10.3 · Multimodal serving
10.3Chapter 10 · Advancements in LLM Serving

Multimodal serving

LLMs ab sirf text tak limited nahi hain — vision-language models (VLMs) aur doosri modalities aage badh rahi hain. Ye models visual aur textual reasoning combine karte hain, aur serving infrastructure ko heterogeneous inputs, bade image tensors aur cross-modal attention ko efficiently handle karna padta hai. Ek distinction clear kar lein: is book me sirf woh language models discuss hote hain jo multimodal input lete hain lekin text tokens generate karte hain standard autoregressive decoder se. Multimodal outputs generate karne wale systems (jaise image ya video generation apps) bilkul alag tareeke se kaam karte hain — aam taur par diffusion-based architectures par — aur book unhe cover nahi karti.

Multimodal input processing kaise hoti hai

Example prompt me image aur text dono content section me pass hote hain: image type ka ek part aur text type ka ek part ("Describe this image."). Prompt template apply karne ke baad image section special tokens se mark hoti hai: <vision_start>, phir <image_pad> placeholders, phir <vision_end>. Input IDs me image placeholder token (151655) 644 baar repeat hota hai — har baar ek image patch ka placeholder.

Model processing ke dauran text token IDs usual tareeke se text embeddings me map hote hain, jabki image placeholder Vision Encoder se aane wali embeddings se replace ho jaata hai. Vision Encoder image ko chhote patches me divide karta hai, har patch ko LLM ke hidden dimension me project karta hai, aur unhe is tarah process karta hai ki patches ek doosre ko attend karke global spatial aur semantic relationships encode kar sakein — final vision embedding ke liye. Matlab dual-stream processing: text stream aur vision stream, dono LLM ke andar milte hain.

Architectural aur system implications

Jaise multimodal models production me aate hain, caching, batching aur streaming ke principles text se aage badhne chahiye. Text tokenization relatively lightweight hoti hai aur aam taur par significant CPU overhead nahi deti. Lekin multimodal inputs ke saath preprocessing me kai computationally demanding, CPU-heavy tasks aate hain: high-resolution images ko raw pixels me convert karna, cropping aur resizing, aur complex tensor transformations — jo LLM shuru hone se pehle sequentially complete hone chahiye. Isse front-loaded computational work hota hai aur early CPU bottleneck banta hai. Agar incoming request rate CPU ki prepare karne ki capacity ko saturate kar de, to powerful GPU idle reh jaata hai. Matlab overall request throughput ab LLM se limit nahi hoti, balki initial CPU-heavy vision-preprocessing stage ki latency aur efficiency se limit hoti hai.

vLLM ke versions 0 aur 1 ke beech ka evolution is bottleneck ko mitigate karne ka achha example hai. Version 1 ka core improvement hai completely asynchronous process adopt karna, taaki CPU-intensive tasks GPU execution se decouple ho jaayein. V0 me multimodal input preprocessing aur API server overhead aksar CPU operations ko block karte the, jisse GPU idle time hota tha. V1 in tasks ko separate CPU processes par offload karta hai jo GPU ke core inference loop ke saath concurrently chalte hain. Is decoupling se CPU overhead minimize hota hai, GPU continuously data se fed rehta hai aur near-full utilization par operate karta hai — result: text aur multimodal workloads dono ke liye significantly higher throughput.

Figure ke hisaab se vLLM V1 do separate processes use karta hai: Process 0 API server, input preprocessing (jahan most heavy multimodal work hota hai) aur output postprocessing ka zimmedar hai; Process 1 ek bilkul separate process hai jo GPU kernel scheduling aur launching ko dedicate hai. Ye separation ensure karta hai ki Process 0 expensive multimodal preprocessing me busy ho to bhi Process 1 continuously GPU kernels launch karta rahe — overall CPU overhead kam hota hai.

Yaad rakho: multimodal serving me bottleneck aksar GPU nahi, CPU hota hai — image preprocessing GPU ko bhooka rakh sakti hai. Isliye text serving ke optimizations ko seedha copy mat karo; preprocessing ko GPU loop se decouple karna yahan sabse bada lever hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Advancements in LLM Serving
← Previous10.2 · Performance profiling strategies→ Next10.4 · Edge AI + multi-LoRA
10.4Chapter 10 · Advancements in LLM Serving

Edge AI + multi-LoRA

Book ka zyada focus large-scale cloud serving par raha hai, lekin ek parallel trend hai: zyada se zyada AI workloads edge devices par serve ho rahe hain. Ye sirf cloud model ko shrink karke device par push karne ka kaam nahi hai — ye hardware advances, model-compression techniques, software runtimes aur architectural patterns ka convergence hai, jo tight power aur memory budgets me real-time intelligence ko feasible banata hai. Isi section me multi-LoRA serving bhi aati hai — ek base model par multiple fine-tuned adapters ko efficiently serve karne ka tareeka.

Edge AI ke teen drivers

Latency: robotics, autonomous driving aur AR/VR jaise applications me latency critical hai — data ko milliseconds me process karke react karna hota hai, aur cloud tak 20–50 ms ka network hop bhi unacceptable hai. Computation edge par move karne se data turant process hota hai, aur safety-critical aur time-sensitive operations ke liye real-time decision making possible hoti hai.

Data locality: raw audio ya video aur sensitive data (medical records, financial details, proprietary industrial data) ko locally process karna essential hai. Aise data ko external cloud servers par bhejna interception ya unauthorized access ka risk badhata hai aur GDPR aur HIPAA jaise stringent data sovereignty aur privacy regulations se conflict karta hai. Edge AI se raw data kabhi premises se bahar nahi jaata.

Cost: modern devices, khaas taur par IoT sensors aur high-resolution cameras, itna data generate karte hain ki network infrastructure overwhelm ho jaata hai aur cloud costs badh jaati hain. Live video streams ko cloud par bhejna network bandwidth aur cloud data transfer aur storage costs me extremely expensive hai. Edge AI data ko locally process aur filter karta hai, aur cloud ko sirf resulting metadata, summarized insights, ya necessary updates bhejta hai — bandwidth consumption significantly kam hoti hai aur continuous, high-volume data transfers par reliance minimize hoti hai.

Edge AI ke enablers

Specialized low-power hardware: kuch saal pehle mobile ya embedded board par deep-learning inference ka matlab tha slow CPUs, limited memory aur sustained workload par collapse hoti battery. Industry AI accelerators ki taraf move hui — specialized chips ya system on a chip (SoC) ke andar dedicated blocks, jo ek kaam exceptionally well karte hain: high-speed, low-precision tensor math. Sabse significant development hai neural processing unit (NPU): CPU ke kuch powerful cores ke ulta, NPU me hazaaron chhote, efficient processing elements hote hain jo unison me operate karte hain. Edge par metric alag hai: raw performance nahi, efficiency king hai — industry-standard metric hai tera-operations per second per watt (TOPS/W). Datacenter server ke paas virtually unlimited power aur cooling hai, lekin battery-operated, fanless edge device ka strict power budget hota hai.

Model compression aur optimization: cloud me compression throughput aur latency optimize karta hai, lekin edge devices par ye aksar functionality ki prerequisite hoti hai — bina in techniques ke modern deep-learning models on-device SRAM ya flash storage me fit hi nahi hote. Quantization, pruning aur distillation ke saath edge-specific techniques bhi hain, jaise KV caching, speculative decoding aur kernel-level optimization.

Heterogeneous compute: aaj ke mobile aur embedded platforms fundamentally heterogeneous hain — har workload ke alag hisse ke liye alag specialized compute units. Ye basically pipeline parallelism hai, lekin alag hardware aur cores ke across: CPU preprocessing karta hai (image resizing, color space conversion, input normalization — branching logic aur memory manipulation, jahan general-purpose cores excel karte hain); NPU neural network ki compute-dense layers execute karta hai (quantization-friendly, high-throughput matrix engines); GPU postprocessing handle karta hai (bounding boxes overlay karna ya augmented visuals real time me render karna). Advanced runtimes subgraph partitioning bhi support karte hain, jahan ek model ki individual layers dynamically alag accelerators ko assign hoti hain — major performance gains, lekin synchronization, memory movement aur scheduling ki nontrivial challenges ke saath.

Thermal-aware scheduling: cloud me server garam ho to fan tez chalti hai. Fanless edge device (jaise pocket me phone ya chhota sensor) par heat performance ko maar deti hai — chip zyada garam ho to physical damage se bachne ke liye drastically slow ho jaata hai (throttling). Intelligent schedulers temperature ko real time me monitor karte hain: agar temperature critical threshold ke paas pahunche, to scheduler dynamically chhote, kam accurate model par switch kar sakta hai ya frame rate kam kar sakta hai; ya workload ko hot main core se cool little core par kuch milliseconds ke liye migrate kar sakta hai, taaki heat dissipate ho. Ye raw peak performance se zyada system stability maintain karta hai.

Edge-cloud hybrid compute: aaj AI workloads devices aur cloud servers ke collaboration par rely karte hain, isolation par nahi. Edge devices immediate response aur strict privacy wale tasks handle karte hain — wake-word detection, lightweight image preprocessing, local video encoding, aur rapid intent understanding ke liye chhota on-device LLM. Ye NPUs aur low-power GPUs ka fayda uthate hain, bina raw inputs ko cloud bhejne ki latency aur data exposure ke. Input filter aur compress hone ke baad (features extract, embeddings compress), cloud heavyweight components bade models se execute karta hai — edge ne input preprocess aur condense kar diya, to cloud kam resources consume karta hai aur faster overall performance deta hai. Adaptive offloading bhi badh raha hai: bandwidth, battery, thermal conditions ya latency requirements ke hisaab se dynamically decide karna ki ek step device par chalega ya cloud me.

Multi-LoRA serving

Companies pehle RAG se proprietary ya domain-specific knowledge model context me laati hain; agla natural step hai fine-tuning — accuracy, coherence aur grounding ko apne unique data, workflows aur communication style se match karna. LoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) ka sabse popular method hai: saare parameters update karne ke bajaye sirf chhote subset ko adapt karta hai, baaki frozen rehte hain. LoRA model architecture me chhote, trainable low-rank layers insert karta hai, taaki task-specific adaptations seekhi ja sakein bina original weights badle — faster, cheaper aur zyada modular fine-tuning.

Multi-LoRA serving ka matlab hai multiple LoRA adapters ko GPU memory me load karke alag requests ko ek hi model serving instance par serve karna. Do key points: pehla, serving ke liye active saare adapters GPU memory me loaded rehte hain, ready to serve — ek-ek karke load nahi hote; inactive ("cold") LoRA zaroorat padne par CPU memory ya disk se load ho sakta hai. Doosra, in requests ko ab bhi continuous batching ke saath batch karna padta hai high GPU utilization aur throughput ke liye — isliye specialized kernels (jaise Punica kernel) develop kiye gaye hain jo main model weights aur multiple alag adapters ke saath calculation process karke sabko combine karte hain. Key benefit: ek single base model instance multiple fine-tuned LoRA adapters concurrently serve kar sakta hai, GPUs ki sankhya kam karte hue — N fine-tuned models ke liye N GPUs ke bajaye sirf 1 GPU — jabki domain-specific behavior ya per-tenant customizations bani rehti hain.

Yaad rakho: multi-LoRA hamesha sahi choice nahi hai. Agar har fine-tuned adapter par heavy traffic hai aur horizontal scaling ke liye multiple model replicas chahiye, to behtar hai har LoRA adapter ko main model me merge karke independently serve karo. Multi-LoRA primarily un cases ke liye hai jahan per-adapter traffic relatively low hai aur har adapter ko independently serve karne se hardware saturate nahi hota.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Advancements in LLM Serving
← Previous10.3 · Multimodal serving→ Next10.5 · RL me model serving
10.5Chapter 10 · Advancements in LLM Serving

RL me model serving

LoRA jaise PEFT methods supervised training se models adapt karte hain, lekin LLMs ke liye reinforcement learning — khaas taur par reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) — ne ek naya frontier khola hai. Labeled data par train karne ke bajaye RLHF human preferences ko incorporate karta hai, taaki models ke responses refine hon. Final outcome sirf sahi answers jaanne wala model nahi hai, balki zyada helpful, polite aur safe model hai — jo human intent se behtar align karta hai. RL-based tuning khaas taur par open-ended generation tasks me valuable hai, jahan correctness bahut subjective hoti hai. LLM training ke stages hain: foundation banana, phir instructions follow karna, phir humans ke saath align karna — RL wahi aakhri stage hai.

RLHF loop me serving: 80% time generation me

Ek popular open source RLHF framework ka estimate hai ki RLHF training time ka 80% sample-generation stage me lagta hai — aur wahi stage model serving hai. Flow do phases me banta hai. Generation (serving) phase: prompts actor model ko bheje jaate hain — actor model RLHF me optimize ho raha current language model hai, jo RL terms me "current policy" hai. Training aage badhne par actor model repeatedly update hota hai, aur "current policy" ka matlab hai uske latest parameters. Actor model multiple replicas par high-throughput serving system se deploy hota hai, taaki downstream evaluation ke liye bade batches me candidate responses efficiently generate ho sakein. Training phase: generated responses ko reward model quality scores deta hai, aur reference model policy gradients compute karne me madad karta hai. Actor model in gradients ke hisaab se update hota hai, aur uske naye weights periodically serving replicas ko sync kar diye jaate hain.

Ye architecture dikhata hai ki serving systems — jo originally inference ke liye bane the — ab RLHF training loop ka integral part hain. Woh scalable, low-latency sampling enable karte hain bade models se, hazaaron concurrent requests ke across. vLLM aur SGLang jaise serving engines is phase me critical role nibhate hain.

Determinism: throughput jitna hi critical

RL serving engines me determinism throughput aur scalability jitna hi critical hai. RLHF me replicas ya runs ke beech chhoti si nondeterminism bhi inconsistent rewards, unstable training aur unreproducible results me propagate ho sakti hai. Matlab reproducible inference performance jitna hi important hai. Recent work dikhata hai ki batch-shape variation jaise subtle implementation details chhote deviations introduce kar sakte hain jo hazaaron RLHF iterations me accumulate hote hain. Generation, reward scoring aur policy updates ko combine karne wale pipelines me aisa drift rewards ya gradient estimates ko destabilize kar sakta hai. Isliye RL ke liye use hone wale modern serving engines sirf serving performance par focus nahi karte — woh batch-invariant deterministic inference par focus karte hain, taaki reproducible token outputs ensure ho sakein.

Yaad rakho: RLHF me serving ek side utility nahi hai — training time ka 80% wahi hai. Agar aap RL training kar rahe ho, to serving engine ka throughput, scalability aur determinism — teenon — training ki speed, stability aur reproducibility tay karte hain. Book yahi baat keh kar khatam hoti hai: hardware architectures badlengi, model families badhengi, nayi modalities aayengi — lekin jo principles aapne seekhe hain, woh rahenge.
SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Advancements in LLM Serving

L1Interactive Lab

KV Cache Size Calculator

Model, precision, context aur batch size chuno — lab batayega ki KV cache kitni GPU memory khayega. Book ka usool: GPU memory lagbhag model size se dugni rakho, warna batch size aur context dono ghut jayenge.

TRY ITModel badlo — KV cache dekho
KV cache ka hisaab

  
Formula (Chapter 5): KV cache per token = 2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × bytes. Book ka example: Llama-2-7B FP16 me 0.5 MB/token — 4096 tokens × batch 16 = 32 GB KV cache, model (14 GB) se bhi bada! Qwen3-14B ka config typical published config hai; cross-check: 72,064 tokens × 0.16 MB ≈ 11 GB — book ke Ch9 measured KV cache se match karta hai.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Challenges When Serving LLMs
← Previous10.5 · RL me model serving→ NextL2 · Arithmetic Intensity Lab


L2Interactive Lab
Arithmetic Intensity Lab


GPU, model aur workload badlo — dekho prefill aur decode ki arithmetic intensity kitni hai, aur workload compute-bound hai ya memory-bandwidth-bound. Decode aksar memory-bound hota hai — yahi serving ka sabse bada sach hai.



  
TRY ITBatch badhao — decode ka verdict badlo

  

    
    
    
  

  

  
Roofline verdict

  
Usool (Chapter 5): arithmetic intensity = FLOPS ÷ data movement. Book ki Table 5-9: matrix size 64 → 21 FLOPS/B, 512 → 170, 4096 → 1365 (lagbhag size ÷ 3). Prefill me poora prompt ek saath process hota hai — bada matrix, compute-bound. Decode me har step par sirf 1 token banta hai — chhota matrix, memory-bound. Batch badhane se decode ka matrix bada hota hai aur intensity badhti hai.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Challenges When Serving LLMs
← PreviousL1 · KV Cache Size Calculator→ NextL3 · Batching Simulator


L3Interactive Lab
Batching Simulator


Batching mode chuno aur requests bhejo — dekho dynamic batching vs continuous batching me throughput aur latency kaise badalti hai. Continuous batching hi aaj ke serving frameworks ki jaan hai.



  
TRY ITMode badlo — 100 requests ka simulation chalao

  

    
    
    
    
  

  

  
Simulation ka natija (100 requests)

  
Usool (Chapter 6): dynamic batching me batch bharne ka wait karna padta hai aur sabse lamba request poore batch ko rokta hai (padding waste). Continuous batching me request khatm hote hi naya request slot me aa jata hai — GPU idle nahi rehta, latency kam aur throughput zyada. Book ka vLLM example: continuous batching + PagedAttention se 8.5x–15x throughput gain milta hai.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Essential Optimization Techniques
← PreviousL2 · Arithmetic Intensity Lab→ NextL4 · Quantization Memory Lab


L4Interactive Lab
Quantization Memory Lab


Model size aur precision chuno — dekho weights kitni memory lete hain, aur har precision ka speed/accuracy trade-off kya hai. Quantization serving ka sabse sasta optimization hai — par har precision har jagah nahi chalti.



  
TRY ITPrecision badlo — memory aur speed dekho

  

    
    
  

  

  
Quantization ka faisla

  
Book ke benchmarks (Chapter 6, Qwen2.5-7B): low concurrency par GPTQ INT4 (W4A16) se ~300% gain, FP8 (W8A8) se ~150% gain — kyunki low batch me bottleneck memory bandwidth hai aur INT4 weights 4x chhote hote hain. High batch par GPTQ ka TTFT baseline se bhi kharab ho jata hai (dequantization overhead, compute abhi bhi 16-bit); FP8 tab behtar hai kyunki activations bhi quantize hoti hain. FP8 sirf Hopper/Blackwell GPUs (H100/H200, L40S) par chalta hai — A100 par nahi.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Essential Optimization Techniques
← PreviousL3 · Batching Simulator→ NextL5 · TTFT & ITL Latency Lab


L5Interactive Lab
TTFT &amp; ITL Latency Lab


Prefill time, per-token decode time aur output length badlo — dekho TTFT, ITL aur end-to-end latency kaise banti hai. Streaming apps me TTFT hi user ko "fast" ya "slow" lagne ka faisla karta hai.



  
TRY ITSliders ghumao — latency dekho

  

    
    
    
    
  

  

  
Latency ka hisaab

  
Formula (Chapter 4): E2E latency = TTFT + ITL × (N − 1), jahan N = output tokens. TTFT = tokenization + prefill + pehla token decode + detokenization. Book ka Ch9 benchmark: Qwen3-14B vLLM par mean TTFT 104.15 ms, mean ITL 43.24 ms, total throughput 474 tok/s. Chhote jawab me TTFT dominate karta hai, lambe jawab me ITL.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Best Practices
← PreviousL4 · Quantization Memory Lab→ NextL6 · Speculative Decoding Lab


L6Interactive Lab
Speculative Decoding Lab


Draft model ki acceptance rate aur speed badlo — dekho speculative decoding kitna speedup deta hai. Ye ekmatra optimization hai jo output quality bilkul same rakhte hue speed badhata hai.



  
TRY ITAcceptance badhao — speedup dekho

  

    
    
    
  

  

  
Speculative decoding ka faisla

  
Usool (Chapter 7): chhota draft model K tokens propose karta hai, bada target model ek hi forward pass me verify karta hai. Accept hue tokens + 1 bonus token milta hai — output bilkul wahi rehta hai jo bina speculation ke milta, kyunki reject hue token ko target model khud sahi karta hai. Book ki salah: draft model target ki family se lo (same tokenizer), draft ko aggressively quantize karo, ya target se distill karke acceptance badhao. Self-drafting (Medusa, EAGLE) bina alag draft model ke yehi kaam karta hai.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Advanced Optimization Techniques

GPU Chooser Lab


GPU aur workload chuno — lab batayega ki model fit hota hai ya nahi, bottleneck kya hai, aur ghante ka kharcha kitna hai. Sahi GPU chunna serving ka sabse mehenga faisla hai.



  
TRY ITGPU badlo — fit ya OOM dekho

  

    
    
    
  

  

  
GPU ka faisla

  
Specs aur costs (Chapter 5, Table 5-4; costs Spring 2026 ke hain, badal sakte hain). Book ke examples: 8B model ke liye A10 kaafi hai (sasta, latency critical nahi ho to); 14B model ke liye L40S achha hai (FP8 support + kaafi memory, single GPU par chal jata hai); 671B MoE model ke liye 8× H200 NVLink ke saath chahiye. Usool: GPU memory lagbhag model size se dugni rakho — weights + KV cache + activations ke liye.

L8Interactive Lab
Framework Chooser Lab


Apni requirements chuno — lab batayega ki vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang ya llama.cpp me se kaunsa framework tumhare use case ke liye sahi hai, aur kyun. Galat framework chunna hafton ki tuning barbaad kar sakta hai.



  
TRY ITRequirements badlo — recommendation dekho

  

    
    
    
  

  

  
Framework recommendation

  
Usool (Chapter 8): vLLM sabse broadly used hai — PagedAttention + continuous batching, "just works", badi community, single-model service ke liye optimized. TensorRT-LLM NVIDIA GPUs par peak performance deta hai par tuning zyada mangta hai. SGLang RadixAttention aur structured generation me mazboot hai — agents aur multi-turn workloads ke liye achha. llama.cpp GGUF quantization ke saath CPU/Apple Silicon par local chalane ke liye hai. Book ka Ch9 project Qwen3-14B ko vLLM par serve karta hai.




SOURCESource: Hands-On LLM Serving and Optimization, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Serving Frameworks

F1End Matter · Interview FAQs
Interview FAQs
LLM serving interviews (current era) ke liye — KV cache se lekar vLLM, disaggregation aur optimization tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 LLM serving kya hai — aur training se kaise alag hai?
LLM serving ka matlab hai trained model ko live users ke liye chalana — request aaye, model jawab de. Training me model weights seekhte hain (backward pass, gradients), serving me sirf forward pass hota hai — weights fixed rehte hain. Serving ki challenges alag hain: latency, throughput, memory aur cost — training ki challenge accuracy aur convergence hoti hai.
Q02 Prefill aur decode phases me kya farak hai?
Prefill me poora input prompt ek saath process hota hai aur pehla token banta hai — ye compute-heavy hota hai kyunki bada matrix multiplication hota hai. Decode me model ek-ek token generate karta hai, har step par poore weights dobara padhne padte hain — ye memory-bandwidth-bound hota hai. Prefill TTFT tay karta hai, decode ITL aur streaming speed tay karta hai.
Q03 KV cache kya hai aur ye speed kyun badhata hai?
KV cache attention ke keys aur values ko store karke rakhta hai, taaki har naye token ke liye purane tokens ko dobara compute na karna pade. Bina KV cache ke har token generation me poori sequence dobara process hoti — bahut slow. Iske badle me GPU memory kharch hoti hai: book ke hisaab se Llama-2-7B FP16 me har token 0.5 MB leta hai, aur 4096 tokens x batch 16 par KV cache 32 GB ho jata hai.
Q04 KV cache ka size kaise estimate karte hain?
Formula hai: KV cache per token = 2 x layers x KV heads x head dimension x bytes per value. Total KV cache = per-token size x (max batch size x max sequence length). Book ka usool hai ki GPU memory lagbhag model size se dugni rakho, taaki weights ke saath KV cache aur activations ke liye bhi jagah bache. GQA aur MLA jaise techniques KV heads kam karke is size ko ghata dete hain.
Q05 Arithmetic intensity kya hai — aur roofline model kya batata hai?
Arithmetic intensity = FLOPS / data movement — matlab har byte padhne par kitni computation hoti hai. Roofline model GPU ki peak compute aur memory bandwidth se ek ridge point nikalta hai: usse kam intensity wala workload memory-bound hai, zyada wala compute-bound. Book ke L40S example me ridge 419 FLOPS/B hai — isse kam intensity par GPU ka poora compute use hi nahi ho pata.
Q06 Decode phase memory-bound kyun hota hai?
Decode me har step par sirf 1 token banta hai, par uske liye model ke saare billion parameters HBM se padhne padte hain — bahut data movement, kam computation. Isliye decode ki arithmetic intensity bahut kam hoti hai aur GPU compute idle rehta hai. Batching se decode ka matrix bada hota hai aur intensity badhti hai; quantization se weights chhote hote hain aur kam bytes padhne padte hain.
Q07 TTFT, ITL aur E2E latency me kya farak hai?
TTFT (Time To First Token) request milne se pehla token aane tak ka time hai — user ko lagta hai system respond kar raha hai. ITL (Inter-Token Latency, TPOT bhi kehte hain) har token ke beech ka time hai — streaming speed. E2E latency = TTFT + ITL x (N - 1), jahan N output tokens hain. Chhote jawab me TTFT dominate karta hai, lambe me ITL.
Q08 Dynamic batching aur continuous batching me kya farak hai?
Dynamic batching me requests ka batch bharne ka wait karte hain, phir poora batch ek saath chalate hain — pehla request wait karta hai aur sabse lamba request sabko rokta hai. Continuous batching me jaise hi ek request khatm hota hai, naya request uske slot me aa jata hai — GPU kabhi idle nahi rehta. Book ke hisaab se vLLM continuous batching aur PagedAttention se 8.5x-15x zyada throughput deta hai.
Q09 PagedAttention kya hai aur ye kyun zaroori hai?
PagedAttention KV cache ko operating system ki tarah pages me baant kar manage karta hai — fixed blocks me allocate karta hai, fragmentation khatm karta hai. Bina iske KV cache ke liye bada contiguous chunk chahiye hota hai aur memory waste hoti hai. Isse zyada requests ek GPU par fit hote hain aur throughput badhta hai. Ye vLLM ki sabse badi innovation hai.
Q10 Chunked prefill kya hai?
Chunked prefill lambe prompt ko chhote chunks me tod kar prefill karta hai, taaki ek lamba prompt decode ko block na kare. Bina chunking ke ek bada prefill saare decode requests ko rok deta hai aur ITL spike ho jata hai. Chunked prefill se prefill aur decode smoothly interleave hote hain — latency predictable rehti hai.
Q11 Quantization kya hai — FP16, INT8, INT4 me kya farak hai?
Quantization weights ko kam precision me store karna hai: FP16 me 2 bytes/param, INT8/FP8 me 1 byte, INT4 me 0.5 byte. Chhote weights ka matlab hai kam memory aur kam memory bandwidth — decode fast hota hai. Trade-off accuracy ka hai: kam precision par thoda loss ho sakta hai. Book ke benchmarks me low concurrency par GPTQ INT4 se ~300% gain aur FP8 se ~150% gain mila.
Q12 Weight-only quantization aur weight-and-activation quantization me kya farak hai?
Weight-only quantization (jaise GPTQ W4A16) sirf weights ko quantize karta hai — activations 16-bit me rehti hain, to compute me koi fayda nahi, sirf memory bandwidth bachta hai. Weight-and-activation (jaise FP8 W8A8) dono ko quantize karta hai — compute bhi fast hota hai. Isliye high batch par GPTQ ka TTFT baseline se bhi kharab ho jata hai (dequantization overhead), jabki FP8 behtar rehta hai.
Q13 FP8 quantization kab use karein — aur kab nahi?
FP8 tab use karo jab high-throughput serving chahiye aur tumhare paas Hopper ya Blackwell GPU (H100/H200, L40S) ho — sirf wahi FP8 Tensor Cores support karte hain. A100 ya purane GPU par FP8 ka fayda nahi milega. Book ke hisaab se FP8 weights aur activations dono par minimal accuracy loss ke saath achha gain deta hai. Low-latency chatbot flows me INT4 kabhi-kabhi behtar hota hai.
Q14 Prefix caching kya hai aur TTFT kaise kam karta hai?
Prefix caching repeated prompt prefixes (jaise system prompt ya few-shot examples) ke KV cache ko save karke rakhta hai, taaki har request me unhe dobara compute na karna pade. Isse TTFT bahut kam ho jata hai — khaas taur par agents aur multi-turn chat me jahan prefix har baar same hota hai. Trade-off memory ka hai: cache ke liye extra GPU memory chahiye hoti hai.
Q15 RadixAttention kya hai?
RadixAttention prefix caching ka smart version hai — ye prefixes ko ek tree (radix tree) me store karta hai, taaki shared prefixes ko alag-alag requests ke beech share kiya ja sake. Ye SGLang framework ki core technique hai. Isse multi-turn conversations aur agents me cache hit rate bahut badh jata hai, kyunki alag users ke prompts bhi aksar same shuruaat share karte hain.
Q16 Speculative decoding kya hai — aur ye accuracy kyun nahi bigadta?
Speculative decoding me chhota draft model aage ke K tokens propose karta hai, aur bada target model ek hi forward pass me unhe verify karta hai. Accept hue tokens plus 1 bonus token milta hai — ek step me kai tokens ban jate hain. Accuracy isliye nahi bigadti kyunki reject hue token ko target model khud apni distribution se sahi karta hai — final output bilkul wahi hota hai jo bina speculation ke milta.
Q17 Speculative decoding ke liye achha draft model kaise chunein?
Draft model chhota aur fast hona chahiye, par acceptance rate bhi zyada honi chahiye — dono ka balance chahiye. Book ki salah: target ki hi family ka model lo (same tokenizer aur pretraining se acceptance badhta hai), draft ko aggressively quantize karo (target fallback ke roop me hamesha hai), ya target se distill karke draft banao. Self-drafting techniques (Medusa, EAGLE) bina alag draft model ke yehi kaam karte hain.
Q18 Prefill-decode disaggregation kya hai?
Prefill-decode disaggregation prefill aur decode ko alag-alag machines (ya GPUs) par chalata hai, kyunki dono ki requirements alag hain — prefill compute-bound hai, decode memory-bound. Isse dono ko alag-alag scale aur optimize kar sakte ho. Challenge KV cache transfer hai: prefill machine se decode machine tak KV cache bhejna padta hai, jo fast interconnect (jaise NVLink ya high-speed network) mangta hai.
Q19 Tensor parallelism aur pipeline parallelism me kya farak hai?
Tensor parallelism ek layer ko multiple GPUs par baant ta hai — har GPU layer ka ek hissa compute karta hai, aur results ko all-reduce se jodte hain. Pipeline parallelism model ki layers ko stages me baant ta hai — har GPU kuch layers sambhalta hai, aur activations ek stage se dusre me jaati hain. Tensor parallel low-latency ke liye achha hai (single request fast), pipeline throughput ke liye — dono ko combine bhi kar sakte ho.
Q20 Data parallelism serving me kab use hota hai?
Data parallelism me model ki poori copy har GPU par hoti hai aur har GPU alag requests serve karta hai — ye throughput badhane ka sabse simple tareeka hai. Ye tab kaam karta hai jab model ek GPU par fit hota hai. Agar model ek GPU par fit hi nahi hota, to pehle tensor ya pipeline parallelism se model baantna padta hai, phir us par data parallelism lagate hain.
Q21 vLLM kya hai — aur ye itna popular kyun hai?
vLLM ek open-source LLM serving framework hai jo PagedAttention aur continuous batching use karta hai. Ye "just works" ke liye famous hai — OpenAI-compatible API, achha throughput out-of-the-box, aur badi active community. Book ka Ch9 project Qwen3-14B ko vLLM par serve karta hai. Ye single-model service ke liye optimized hai.
Q22 vLLM vs TensorRT-LLM vs SGLang — kaunsa kab chunein?
vLLM chuno jab general-purpose cloud serving chahiye aur jaldi setup karna ho — sabse safe default hai. TensorRT-LLM chuno jab NVIDIA GPU par peak performance chahiye aur tuning ka time hai. SGLang chuno jab multi-turn chat, agents ya structured JSON output ho — iska RadixAttention prefix caching me sabse aage hai. llama.cpp chuno jab CPU ya laptop par local chalana ho.
Q23 llama.cpp kab use karna chahiye?
llama.cpp tab use karo jab koi datacenter GPU nahi hai — laptop, edge device ya CPU-only server par model chalana ho. Ye GGUF quantization ke saath models ko CPU aur Apple Silicon par chalata hai. Throughput vLLM jaisa nahi milega, par portability aur low cost sabse zyada hai. Small models aur personal use ke liye ideal hai.
Q24 GPU chunne ke liye sabse important specs kaunse hain?
Chaar cheezein dekho: memory capacity (model + KV cache fit hona chahiye), memory bandwidth (decode speed tay karta hai), compute TFLOPS (prefill speed), aur interconnect (multi-GPU ke liye NVLink). Book ka usool: GPU memory lagbhag model size se dugni rakho. Book ke examples: 8B ke liye A10, 14B ke liye L40S, 671B MoE ke liye 8x H200 NVLink ke saath.
Q25 H100 SXM aur H100 NVL me kya farak hai?
H100 SXM me zyada compute hai (FP16 1979 TFLOPS) par kam memory (80 GB) aur kam bandwidth (3.35 TB/s). H100 NVL me compute thoda kam hai (1671 TFLOPS) par zyada memory (94 GB) aur zyada bandwidth (3.9 TB/s). Compute-heavy prefill workloads ke liye SXM behtar hai, lambi context aur bade batch (memory-heavy) workloads ke liye NVL. Sirf FLOPS dekh kar GPU mat chuno.
Q26 A100 par FP8 kyun nahi chalta?
FP8 Tensor Cores sirf Hopper (H100/H200) aur Blackwell architecture me hain — A100 Ampere architecture ka hai, usme FP8 hardware support hi nahi hai. A100 par FP8 code chalega par FP16 speed se fast nahi hoga. Isliye A100 par quantization ke liye INT8 ya INT4 (weight-only) use karte hain. GPU khareedne se pehle check karo ki tumhari quantization strategy us hardware par supported hai ya nahi.
Q27 Model loading ke bottlenecks kya hain?
Pehla bottleneck hai weights ko disk se GPU memory me load karna — bade models me ye time lagta hai. Dusra hai KV cache ke liye jagah reserve karna — sirf weights fit hona kaafi nahi hai. Teesra hai cold start: pehla request aane par model load, tokenizer aur framework init sab ek saath hota hai. Book ke hisaab se Qwen3-14B vLLM par 38.5 GiB leta hai — model 27.5 GB aur KV cache 11 GB.
Q28 Profiling se kya pata chalta hai — aur kab profile karein?
Profiling batata hai ki time kahan ja raha hai: prefill me, decode me, kernel launch me, ya memory transfer me. Optimize karne se pehle hamesha profile karo — bina measurement ke optimization guesswork hai. Book ka approach: pehle TTFT aur ITL measure karo, phir bottleneck par hi optimize karo. Aam bottlenecks hain: chhota batch (memory-bound decode), lamba prompt (prefill-heavy), ya chhota KV cache (recomputation).
Q29 Prompt length TTFT ko kaise affect karti hai?
Prefill time prompt length ke saath badhta hai — lamba prompt matlab zyada computation pehle token se pehle. Isliye TTFT kam karne ke liye prompt chhota karo, prefix caching lagao, ya prefill-decode disaggregation use karo. Book ke Ch9 benchmark me Qwen3-14B ka mean TTFT 104 ms tha — ye prompt length aur concurrency par depend karta hai.
Q30 Concurrency badhane se latency aur throughput par kya asar padta hai?
Concurrency badhane se throughput badhta hai (GPU zyada utilize hota hai), par har request ki latency badh sakti hai — khaas taur par TTFT, kyunki prefill ke liye queue me wait karna padta hai. Book ke quantization benchmarks me high concurrency par GPTQ INT4 ka TTFT baseline se bhi kharab ho gaya. Isliye concurrency ko SLA ke hisaab se tune karo, blindly max mat karo.
Q31 Agents aur RAG workloads ki serving me kya khaas hai?
Agents aur RAG me ek user request par model ko kai baar call karna padta hai — tool calls, retrieval steps, multi-turn reasoning. Isliye per-call latency bahut matter karti hai: chhoti latency kai calls me multiply ho jati hai. Prefix caching (repeated system prompt) aur low-latency quantization (INT4) yahan sabse zyada fayda dete hain. Book ke Ch4 me agents aur RAG ko best-practices chapter me alag se cover kiya gaya hai.
Q32 KV cache quantization kab use karein?
KV cache quantization tab use karo jab lambi context ya bada batch chahiye aur GPU memory kam pad rahi ho — KV cache ko FP8/INT8 me store karke memory bacha sakte ho. Par dhyaan rakho: sirf KV cache quantize karne se latency kam nahi hoti, kyunki attention calculation abhi bhi high precision me hoti hai aur dequantization overhead aata hai. Poora fayda tab milta hai jab quantized attention kernel bhi use karo.
Q33 MoE (Mixture of Experts) models ki serving me kya alag hai?
MoE models me har token sirf kuch experts ko activate karta hai — jaise 671B parameter wale model me bhi per-token compute kam hota hai. Par saare experts ki weights memory me rakhni padti hain, isliye memory requirement bahut zyada hoti hai. Serving me experts ko multiple GPUs par baanta jata hai. Book ke hisaab se 671B MoE ke liye 8x H200 NVLink ke saath chahiye hota hai.
Q34 Serving cost kaise estimate karein — aur kaise kam karein?
Cost = GPU hourly price x GPUs x hours. GPU price book me Spring 2026 ka hai: H100 ~$6.2/h, L40S ~$2.25/h, A10 <$1.25/h. Cost kam karne ke tareeke: chhota model use karo (distillation), quantization karo, batching badhao (GPU utilization), prefix caching lagao, aur sahi size ka GPU chuno — 8B model ko H100 par chalana paise barbaad karna hai.
Q35 Model routing kya hai aur kab use hota hai?
Model routing har request ko sahi model par bhejta hai — simple sawal chhote/saste model par, mushkil sawal bade model par. Isse cost aur latency dono kam hote hain bina quality ghataye. Routing ke liye chhota classifier ya rule-based logic use hota hai. Book ke system design chapter me routing ko serving architecture ka core component bataya gaya hai.
Q36 Emerging directions — LLM serving ka future kis taraf ja raha hai?
Book ka aakhri chapter batata hai ki field bahut tezi se badal raha hai: naye attention mechanisms (MLA jaise), naye hardware (FP4 support, naye accelerators), disaggregated architectures, aur agent-native serving. Har naye technique ko usi lens se dekho jo book ne sikhaya: arithmetic intensity, KV cache memory, aur TTFT/ITL — fundamentals same rehte hain, techniques badalti rehti hain.
